components.css: .ds-tabbar { font-family: "Barlow", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); height: 4.25rem; margin-top: 2rem; background: var(--navy, #24305e); color: var(--navy-muted, #c3c9e4); } .ds-tabbar a { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.2rem; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-tabbar a[aria-current=page] { color: var(--navy-ink, #fff); } .ds-tabbar a:active { opacity: 0.7; } .ds-tabbar a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--navy-ink, #fff); outline-offset: -4px; } .ds-tabbar svg { width: 1.25rem; height: 1.25rem; } .ds-tab-scan { justify-content: flex-end !important; padding-bottom: 0.55rem; color: var(--navy-ink, #fff) !important; } .ds-scan-disc { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 3.5rem; height: 3.5rem; margin-top: -1.6rem; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--violet, #6b3fa0); color: var(--violet-ink, #fff); border: 0.3rem solid var(--navy, #24305e); box-shadow: 0 0.35rem 0.8rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--navy, #24305e) 60%, #000 40%); box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-scan-disc svg { width: 1.6rem; height: 1.6rem; } .ds-tab-scan:active .ds-scan-disc { filter: brightness(0.88); }

narrative.overview:
Kereta is the dealer service booklet that lives in the glovebox, rebuilt for a phone held at a workshop counter. Every vehicle opens on a navy booklet cover carrying its name and a black number plate; under it sits a cream, ruled page of schedule rows; every logged visit lands in the history as a slightly crooked rubber stamp in violet ink. The whole interface is paper, ink and one stamp colour. Depth comes from rules and covers, not from floating cards.

Density is that of a printed form: rows at least 2.875rem tall, hairline rules between them, a 2px ink rule heading each ruled block, and tabular figures wherever a number sits in a column. The type is a single sturdy grotesque (Barlow) set at medium weight, with a typewriter face (Courier Prime) reserved for the stamps alone, so the stamp reads as a different instrument from the page it is pressed onto. The world refuses the category's soft cards with coloured status dots: status is told in words, with an icon, in a colour, on a ruled line.

At night the booklet keeps its structure. The ground turns navy-black, the page a little lighter, the rules dark slate, and the ink a warm cream; navy covers, black plates and violet stamps all survive the switch.
keyCharacteristics: Navy booklet cover (shell, vehicle covers, tab bar, selected segment) over a cream ruled page.
Ruled hairlines under a 2px ink head rule for every list, table and schedule.
Violet is the only accent: stamp ink, the primary action, links, focus, selection.
Barlow throughout; Courier Prime uppercase only inside stamps.
Small 4px corners; plates are black badges; stamps are the one softer, tilted shape.
Everything sized in rem so the Text size preference scales the whole booklet.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only accent. It marks what the user can do (primary action, links, focus) and what they have done (stamps). Nothing decorative is violet.

rules.name: The Red-Means-Late Rule
rules.body: Red and amber-brown are status colours and nothing else. Errors share the red because they are also "act now"; no other surface uses them.

rules.name: The Words-Icon-Colour Rule
rules.body: A flagged status (overdue, due soon, unknown) is always colour plus an icon plus words: circle-cross for overdue, clock for due soon, pencil for unknown. Colour alone never carries a status. An "ok" row is words only, in faded ink.

rules.name: The Typewriter-Only-In-Stamps Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime appears inside a stamp and nowhere else. Every other figure, including dates, odometer readings and money in rows and totals, is Barlow with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Rem Rule
rules.body: Every size, padding and target is in rem, so the Text size preference (`html[data-text-size]`: default 100%, `large` 112.5%, `larger` 125%) scales the whole booklet. Px is allowed only for border widths and hairlines.

rules.name: The 44 Rule
rules.body: Every touch target is at least 2.75rem (44px at 100% text size): text links, crumbs, segments, quiet links and the "more" link. Rows, inputs and buttons are 2.875rem; profile rows 3.25rem.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Raised Rule
rules.body: Lists, tables, schedules, totals, facts and profile rows are ruled blocks on the page colour, headed by a 2px ink rule; they never get a drop shadow. The one shadow belongs to the Scan disc.

dos: Do open each vehicle with its navy cover and plate, then a ruled page; keep the cover-over-page radius split (top on the cover, bottom on the page).
Do head every list, table or schedule with a 2px ink rule and separate rows with 1px `rule` hairlines on the `page` colour.
Do show every flagged status as colour plus icon plus words: overdue red with the circle-cross, due-soon amber-brown with the clock, unknown violet with the pencil.
Do keep every touch target at least 2.75rem, and rows, inputs and buttons at 2.875rem.
Do size everything in rem so `html[data-text-size]` (100% / 112.5% / 125%) scales the booklet.
Do theme through the tokens only: `html[data-theme]` is `system`, `light` or `dark`, and the dark tokens hang off the resolved `html[data-scheme="dark"]`, defined once.
Do let booklets run edge to edge below 30rem, and hold the tab bar's tabs to the 36rem column on wide screens.
Do use tabular figures for dates, km and money in rows, totals, facts and cover sublines.
donts: Don't use soft floating cards or coloured status dots; status lives on a ruled line, in words.
Don't use Courier Prime outside a visit stamp.
Don't add a second accent; violet is the only one, and red and amber-brown mean status.
Don't add drop shadows to blocks or rows; the raised Scan disc is the only shadow.
Don't round beyond 4px except the stamp, the Scan disc and the small line-item tag.
Don't size type, padding or targets in px; px is for border widths only.
